name: Stonier Wines
signature: One of the Peninsula's founding estates, planted in 1978, grown-up, unflashy, with some of the oldest Chardonnay vines in the region.
editorNote:
Stonier was planted in 1978 by Brian and Noel Stonier, making it one of the earliest established estates on the Peninsula. The site has been through ownership changes since, it now sits within a larger wine group, but the winemaking credentials have held. The Reserve Chardonnay and KBS Vineyard Pinot Noir remain reference-point wines for what the region can do with its two flagship varieties.

The cellar door reflects the winery's philosophy: no wedding marquee, no sculpture trail, no cheese board dressed for Instagram. What you get is serious wine in a grown-up room, presented by staff who know the portfolio. Ask for the winemaker's-list flight if you want to work through the range properly, it covers a broader selection than the standard pour and gives you a better read on the estate's full scope.

This is the cellar door for wine people who want conversation about what's in the glass rather than a polished sensory experience. Wear what you'd wear to a good restaurant, not what you'd wear to a Sunday market.

visiting.tastingNote: Walk-ins welcome daily for groups under 6 (final tastings 4pm); tasting fee redeemable on wine purchase; complimentary for Wine Club members. Reservations required for groups of 6+. Dogs welcome on the lawn.

editorVerdict: Stonier is the Peninsula's original benchmark. Brian Stonier planted his vines in 1978 when 'Mornington Peninsula wine' was not yet a phrase anyone used outside this paddock. The estate returned to local family ownership in December 2022. The KBS Vineyard Chardonnay is still the Peninsula reference bottle for that variety - three decades of track record don't lie.
whyWeGo: When you want a cellar door built around the wine rather than the experience around the wine, Stonier is the answer on the Peninsula.
ifOnlyOneThing: Ask specifically for the Reserve flight, the Reserve Chardonnay and KBS Pinot Noir are the wines that make the visit worthwhile.

faq.q: Does Stonier Wines take walk-ins or do you need to book?
faq.a: Walk-ins welcome daily 11am–5pm for groups under 6. Reservations required for larger groups.

faq.q: Does Stonier Wines have a restaurant?
faq.a: No formal restaurant. Local charcuterie platters from Long Paddock and Main Ridge Dairy cheeses are available at the cellar door.

faq.q: Are dogs allowed at Stonier Wines?
faq.a: Confirmed yes - dogs are welcome on the lawn.
